LESSON: MECHANICAL PROPERTIES OF MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS
Strand: Mechanics and Thermal Physics
Topic 1.3: Mechanical Properties of Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mechanical Properties of Materials, part of Mechanics and Thermal Physics in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS.

Key inquiry question: Why does a string snap easily as compared to a spring? 2. Why is it important to study the mechanical properties of materials?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss with peers the mechanical properties of locally available materials and share their findings. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss with peers the mechanical properties of locally available materials and share their findings. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/ point/sign/write) during the discussion,
2. Carry out activities to demonstrate the mechanical properties (ductility, malleability, elasticity, brittleness, strength, hardness, stiffness and any other 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mechanical Properties of Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the learner develops the speaking skill as they discuss the mechanical properties

of locally available materials.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner develops the skill of interpretation and inference as they

14

explore problems by creating different possible solutions and their pros and cons while using mathematical

relationships to determine tensile stress, tensile strain and modulus of elasticity of materials.

15

Values

• Responsibility: the learner shows accountability as they take care of apparatus used to perform experiments while

determining the constant of elasticity, tensile stress, tensile strain and modulus of elasticity of material.

• Respect: the learner shows etiquette as they display humility during group discussions on mechanical

properties of materials and their relevance in day-to-day life.

• Integrity: the learner develops virtue of honesty as they present genuine results that reflect the actual findings

and observations of group discussions and practical activities on mechanical properties of materials.
